newsitem.title: USA: Kmart completes repayment of $1.2 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Kmart completes repayment of $1.2 bln loan.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Thursday it has completed repayment of a $1.2 billion loan taken out last year as part of a refinancing that helped avert a financial crisis for the retailer.

"At the time of the refinancing, Kmart said it intended to pay this obligation down within one year," said Marvin Rich, executive vice president of finance, planning, and administration said in a news release. "These actions make good on that promise one quarter ahead of schedule, providing further evidence of continued improvement in Kmart's financial health."
With completion of the loan payment, Kmart's long-term debt to total capitalization ratio falls to 35 percent on a pro forma basis, down from 51 percent at the end of 1995, the retailer said.
The loan was not due until 1999.

Kmart also said its interest costs are expected to trend lower in 1997, due both to a lower level of borrowings and lower anticipated interest rates on the company's $2.5 billion revolving credit facility.

As a result of improved earnings performance in fiscal 1996, the ongoing rate of the revolving credit facility will decline by 100 basis points when Kmart files its 10K report for fiscal 1996 with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Kmart said.

The revolving credit facility itself, which is used primarily to fund short term working capital needs of the business, was entirely paid down in mid-December and remains untapped today, indicating stronger cash flows within the company's operations, Kmart said.

"While the overall liquidity of Kmart, as measured by cash and available borrowing capacity, continues to run ahead of management's expectations of improvement, we will continue to pursue the company's goal of returning to investment grade," Kmart said.
